title: U.S. House · Florida's 20th District
area: Parts of Broward County, including Weston and surrounding South Florida communities, under Florida's 2026 congressional map.

context.text: Florida's U.S. House elections use a new congressional map for 2026; Gov. Ron DeSantis signed the new district boundaries into law on May 4, 2026.

Incumbent Rep. Debbie Wasserman Schultz (D) won the Democratic primary on August 18, 2026, defeating Luther Campbell, Sheila Cherfilus-McCormick, Dale Holness, and Elijah Manley. Brent Andersen won the Republican primary. Kedner Maxime advanced as the Independent Party of Florida nominee after that primary was canceled.

summary.text: Debbie Wasserman Schultz is the incumbent Democratic U.S. Representative, first elected to the House in 2005. She previously served in the Florida House and Senate and chaired the Democratic National Committee from 2011 to 2016.

background.text: Born in Queens, New York, in 1966; graduated from Half Hollow Hills High School East in 1984 and earned a bachelor's degree (1988) and master's degree (1990) in political science from the University of Florida.
Served in the Florida House of Representatives from 1992 to 2000 and the Florida Senate from 2000 to 2004 before her election to Congress.
Chaired the Democratic National Committee from 2011 to 2016; is Florida's first Jewish member of Congress.

record.text: Serves as Ranking Member of the House Appropriations Committee for the 2025–2026 Congress, and also sits on the Agriculture and Energy and Water subcommittees.
Authored the Virginia Graeme Baker Pool and Spa Safety Act, enacted in 2007, and sponsored the PROTECT Our Children Act, creating a federal law enforcement effort to protect children.
Introduced the EARLY Act to increase breast cancer education and awareness, which was enacted as part of the Affordable Care Act in 2010.
Introduced the Rape Survivor Child Custody Act, encouraging states to allow termination of a rapist's parental rights; signed into law in 2015.

summary.text: Brent Andersen is an insurance professional and Republican Party leader running against incumbent Debbie Wasserman Schultz, campaigning on lowering property insurance costs and the cost of living.

background.text: Works as an insurance professional in South Florida; describes himself as a businessman and Republican Party leader.
Endorsed by the Sun Sentinel, Miami Herald, and Log Cabin Republicans PAC, according to his Candidate Connection survey.

priorities.text: Says his experience in the insurance industry drives his focus on market-based solutions to lower property insurance premiums and housing costs.
Says he will bring private-sector experience and fiscal responsibility to Congress to grow jobs and economic opportunity.
Says he will defend limited government, the Second Amendment, secure borders, and parental rights.

positions.summary: Says he will defend the Second Amendment.
Lists strong borders and public safety among his top policy priorities.
